transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Arcadia - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Arcadia - Infra Lead), Anita Sharma (Arcadia - Security), Leo Park (Arcadia - PM)

Summary: quick alignment on POC scope and timeline; key metrics are p95 latency <= 350ms for short requests (<=256 tokens), throughput target 80 req/s steady-state for batch of 4, and quality measured by F1 on labeled dataset >= 0.86. Plan: kickoff week 7/22, infra access 1 week before, benchmark run 8/3-8/7, midpoint review 8/12, exec readout 8/21.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour, maybe a hair over. I'll do quick intros and then pass to Priya for the technical asks.
00:18 Maya: hi thanks, Maya here, head of ML at Arcadia. We run a document extraction product, want to test Redwood for inference on our customer documents, mostly 200-800 token texts, some longer.
00:34 Carlos: Carlos, infra. we care about VPC peering and egress, and also cost predictability.
00:45 Anita: Anita, security. we'll want SOC2/ISO docs, KMS details, and an audit log walkthrough.
00:58 Jordan: great, thanks. Priya, can you run through what we'll need for the POC and the typical milestones?
01:08 Priya: yeah sure. High-level, we propose a 4-week POC: kickoff, access/setup, benchmark runs, midpoint review, then exec readout. Baselines we'll capture: latency (p50/p95), throughput, token cost, and accuracy on your labeled set. For the benchmark we'll need sample traffic and some ground truth labels.
01:35 Leo: for our success criteria top-level, we want: p95 < 350ms for short requests, throughput 80 req/s for concurrency of 8 with batching, and extraction accuracy F1 >= 0.86 comp to our current model. If we can't meet those we probably won't move to dedicated.
02:02 Priya: understoood. couple clarifying q's — what's your typical batch size and size distribution? you said 200-800 tokens but is there a long tail?
02:16 Maya: we have a long tail — about 5% of docs are 1.2k-2k tokens. Most are under 500. For benchmarks we can filter to typical workload and also run a separate long-tail test.
02:31 Priya: perfect. For infra, we support three options: hosted Redwood (fastest to start, limited VPC controls), dedicated (reserved capacity on GPUs, more predictable throughput), and private/VPC (customer-managed, fully isolated). Given your security posture what are you leaning?
02:55 Anita: goal is private or VPC — we need KMS integration and control plane isolation. Hosted is ok for an eval but prod needs private. For POC we prefer to test in a VPC peering setup to validate networking.
03:12 Jordan: ok noted. Carlos, can you confirm your networking constraints and timeline?
03:19 Carlos: we can open up peering, but we'll need a runbook for exact IP ranges and pre-shared keys. we have change window windows on 7/21 so ideally access by 7/22 is fine. We'll need a list of minimal ACLs.
03:36 Priya: we'll provide a minimal access checklist: service account keys, egress rules, S3 read bucket, and a small bastion if needed. we'll also list ports and CIDRs.
03:45 Maya: on success metrics, also want to measure hallucination rates and some business KPIs — looks like you have a quality monitoring toolkit?
03:55 Priya: yes we have Redwood Optimize suggestions, and quality monitoring that ties to prompt sets and evals. For hallucination we recommend specific prompt templates and a reranking step; we'll measure false positive/negative per sample.
04:10 Leo: budget question — what's the estimated token cost for a 4-week benchmark? we need a ballpark to get internal ok.
04:20 Jordan: we'll send a pricing sheet. rough back-of-envelope depends on model — for an open quantized model it's lower, for large LLMs higher. We'll include dedicated vs hosted comparisons.
04:33 Maya: also, we run throughput tests with sustained bursts. Can Redwood handle continuous 80 req/s for several minutes without degradation?
04:42 Priya: yes, with dedicated capacity and correct batching we can meet that. We'll design the benchmark to ramp and steady-state, and measure latency p95 across the window.

06:00 [timestamp jump to technical discussion after short break]
06:05 Priya: technical details for benchmarking: we'll need your sample dataset (5k rows recommended), a set of labeled examples (500-1k for accuracy eval), and a traffic generator script signature. We'll provide a harness that runs concurrent clients and reports per-request lat/throughput.
06:30 Carlos: we can provide a 5k sample by 7/20 and we have a test account for S3. We'll provision an IAM role but need the exact policy.
06:42 Priya: we'll share the minimal IAM policy. Also, for VPC peering we'll supply subnet ranges and a list of endpoints. Expect a doc from us today.
06:55 Anita: security questions — audit logs retention, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed keys?
07:05 Priya: yes for private deployments we support KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys; we also produce detailed audit logs and can configure retention windows depending on plan. We'll attach SOC2/ISO artifacts and a security FAQ.
07:20 Anita: any known compliance gaps we should be aware of?
07:24 Priya: none in general; we'll run ZTA (zero trust) recommendations. For PII-handling we also suggest tokenization suggestions. We'll follow up with the security engineering team if there are deeper questions.

09:00 Jordan: let's get concrete on milestones and dates. Proposed timeline: kickoff 7/22, access/setup done by 7/29, benchmark week 8/3-8/7, midpoint review 8/12, exec readout 8/21. That gives two weeks buffer and time for fixes. Thoughts?
09:25 Maya: that aligns with our internal calendar; CTO wants results for exec readout end of August so 8/21 is fine.
09:33 Carlos: confirm we can do access by 7/22 — we have a change window 7/21 so yes.
09:39 Priya: great. For the kickoff we'll do a 60-90 minute session: intro to Redwood infra, access checklist, and runbook for benchmark. We'll ask Arcadia to share LUT (workload template) and sample dataset during that meeting.
09:55 Leo: can we include product engineering in the kickoff? they'd like to see the pipeline for integrating real-time inference.
10:02 Jordan: absolutely. We'll invite an engineer from Redwood infra and a solutions architect.

12:10 [benchmark-specific clarifications]
12:15 Priya: benchmarks we'll run: small request latency (<=256 tokens), medium (256-800), and long-tail (>1k). For each we'll test with batching factors 1,4,8 and two quantized model variants. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and accuracy/F1. Do you have an internal baseline numbers to compare?
12:40 Maya: our current in-house baseline p95 is ~420ms for small requests, F1 is 0.84 on extraction. So target is to beat latency and match or exceed accuracy.
12:52 Priya: good. We'll set up a benchmark spreadsheet with the metrics and expected thresholds and share it.

15:00 [discussion around dedicated vs hosted]
15:05 Jordan: quick note: for the POC we can do hosted with VPC peering emulation or a VPC test. Dedicated gives more realistic capacity results for throughput. If your prod plan is private, we recommend running POC in VPC peering to validate networking and then a short dedicated run to validate throughput.
15:28 Carlos: ok prefer VPC peering for the POC and then a quick dedicated validation if things look promising.

17:00 [risks and mitigation]
17:05 Anita: risk: keys and audit logs — need clarity on retention and access controls. Another risk: long-tail performance under heavy load.
17:17 Priya: mitigation: we'll provide a security checklist, and run dedicated long-tail stress tests. Also we have automatic fallback policies if a heavy request would impact latency SLOs.
17:35 Maya: operational question — how does Redwood handle model rollouts and version pinning? We need predictable model versions in prod.
17:45 Priya: you can pin model versions, do canary and A/B rollouts; Redwood console gives per-route dashboards and tracing for regression analysis. We'll demonstrate in the kickoff.

20:00 [recap and next steps]
20:10 Jordan: recap — agreed success criteria: p95 < 350ms (short), throughput 80 req/s, F1 >= 0.86. Timeline: kickoff 7/22, access by 7/29, benchmark 8/3-8/7, midpoint 8/12, exec readout 8/21. Action items assigned as in the chat. We'll send pricing and SOC2/ISO docs by tomorrow.
20:35 Maya: sounds good. Please include the benchmark spreadsheet template and the harness instructions.
20:42 Priya: will do. we'll also share the exact network CIDRs and minimal IAM policy today.
20:50 Anita: I'll compile security questions and send them by 7/16.
21:00 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites and next steps.
21:07 [call ended]
